name: Aralle-Tabulahan
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_quote: Stress in A-T is regular and predictable. Apart from three conditions which place stress on other syllables, stress in this language always falls on the penultimate. (38) [ˈtama] 'to enter' [paˈtama] 'to cause to enter' [kupaˈtama] 'I cause to enter' [lakupaˈtama] 'I will cause to enter' Rule 1 - Stress placement S --> [+stress] / _ S ]word

audit.reasoning: The fixed-strict penultimate coding (penultimate stress) rests on the only existing phonology of Aralle-Tabulahan, a 52-page primary SIL description by the fieldworker (McKenzie 1991), which we hold in full; the deciding sentence and example (38) are verbatim on p.110, the three exceptions on pp.110-111 and footnote 1 on p.147 as cited. The exceptions (distal vocatives, unstressed enclitics outside the stress domain, fast-speech glide shift, stative-intensification double stress) are pragmatic/clitic/rapid-speech effects that do not disturb a word-domain penultimate coding. No later grammar, dissertation or instrumental study exists per Glottolog (2 descriptive refs) and web search, so nothing is added to the list of works to obtain and nothing was downloaded (the open SIL PDF is already.

sources.citation: McKenzie, Robin 1991, "Phonology of Aralle-Tabulahan", in Rene van den Berg (ed.), Sulawesi phonologies, Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 12, Ujung Pandang: SIL, pp. 110-111 (stress section 3.1) and p. 147 (note 1). Accessed as the SIL scanned PDF …
